data.name: Lahab
data.long_meaning: In the Quran, Lahab refers to the name of an idolater, who was a contemporary of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). His name means 'the Flame'. He was a father of five sons whom he used to worship idols. One day, he saw Prophet Ibrahim destroying his idols. Lahab and his sons then went to Ibrahim and taunted him for his actions. Ibrahim replied to them with the wisdom of monotheism. Lahab and his sons were so infuriated by Ibrahim's words that they threw him into a fire. But Allah Almighty saved Ibrahim, and Lahab and his sons were consumed by the fire instead. This story is a reminder of the power and might of Allah.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes faith and resilience in the face of adversity.
data.numerology_meaning: Independent, ambitious, and a natural born leader.

in_arabic.name: لَهَب
in_arabic.meaning: لَهَب يعني النار الشديدة أو اللهب
in_arabic.long_meaning: لَهَب هو اسم مشتق من الفعل 'لَهَبَ' الذي يعني إشعال النار أو اللهب الشديد. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم لوصف النار الحارة أو الشعلة القوية. وفي سياق الأسماء الإسلامية، قد يُرتبط بالشخص الذي يحمل قلبًا حارًا أو عاطفة قوية في الإيمان أو العمل الصالح.

in_urdu.name: لہب
in_urdu.meaning: لہب کا مطلب ہے شدید نرمی یا گرم جوشی
in_urdu.long_meaning: لہب ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے 'شديد نرمی' یا 'گرم جوشی'۔ یہ نام ان شخصیتوں کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو گرم جوشی اور شدت کے ساتھ کام کرتے ہیں، یا ان کی شخصیت میں ایک خاص قسم کی جوش و خروش موجود ہوتی ہے۔

in_hindi.name: लहब
in_hindi.meaning: लहब का अर्थ है प्रबल ज्वाला या तीव्र गर्मी
in_hindi.long_meaning: लहब एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है 'प्रबल ज्वाला' या 'तीव्र गर्मी'। यह नाम उन व्यक्तियों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जिनमें एक विशेष प्रकार की ऊर्जा और उत्साह होता है, जो उनके काम और गतिविधियों में प्रतिबिंबित होता है।

in_pashto.name: لَهَب
in_pashto.meaning: لَهَب د قوي اورښت يا تودې معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: لَهَب د عربي اصل يو نوم دی چې د 'قوي اورښت' يا 'تودې' معنی لري. دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کېږي چې په خپل کار او ژوند کې د يو خاص ډول تودې او جوش لرونکي وي.

data.cultural_impact: The name Lahab has its origins in ancient Arabian culture, specifically mentioned in the Quran. It is the name of a man who challenged the monotheistic beliefs of Prophet Ibrahim, and the story of their encounter serves as a reminder of the importance of faith and the rejection of idolatry in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Lahab holds a profound spiritual significance as it serves as a warning against following the path of disbelief and idolatry. It is a reminder of the importance of trusting in Allah's power and wisdom, and the dangers of straying from the path of monotheism. The story of Prophet Ibrahim and Lahab also highlights the courage and steadfastness of Ibrahim in the face of adversity and the power of Allah's protection and guidance.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Ishaq's Sirat Rasul Allah (Biography of the Prophet), chapter 38, mentions Lahab ibn Qays as a Meccan idolater and an enemy of Muhammad. He was a cousin of Abu Lahab, also an opponent of Muhammad.
historical_references.context: Pre-Islamic Arabian culture and religion, specifically Meccan polytheism and opposition to the emergence of monotheistic beliefs.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Hisham's Al-Sirah Al-Nabawiyyah (The Life of the Prophet), chapter 10, describes Lahab ibn Abd al-Muttalib as a paternal uncle of Muhammad who initially supported him but later became an enemy and was exiled from Mecca.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic history, specifically the early years of the Prophet Muhammad's mission in Mecca and his struggles against opposition from the Meccan community.
